objections.claim: The spec asserts the widened pattern "declines to match `.faff/configuration…`" because "the widened class requires a `.` separator before each extra segment," and that "other `config`-prefixed words — not matched." The second claim is false. Because the trailing `(?:\.ya?ml)?` is optional and `\b` follows it, the pattern matches bare `.faff/config` wherever a word boundary holds after `config` — i.e. before any non-word character. So `.faff/config-notes.md`, `.faff/config.lock`, `.faff/config.json`, `.faff/config-helper.sh` all match via the zero-segments/empty-extension arm; the `(?:\.[\w-]+)*` group is almost entirely dead weight. The `configuration` claim happens to be true (no boundary between `g` and `u`), but the spec's stated mechanism is not what produces the behaviour, and the "other config-prefixed words — not matched" edge-case line is wrong as written.
objections.evidence: §3 WHAT, "Design decision — the widened pattern" and §4 "Edge cases" (`\.faff\/config(?:\.[\w-]+)*(?:\.ya?ml)?\b`; "not matched: the widened class requires a `.` separator before each extra segment").
objections.predicted_consequence: the DONE-derived case table (§8: "asserts the match/no-match case table above") is built from the spec's inaccurate edge-case prose and omits the hyphenated/dotted-suffix cases the pattern actually matches; a future reader trusting the spec's precision rationale will mis-predict the lint's behaviour, and the first `.faff/config-*` false positive (or deliberate flag) will look like a regex bug rather than documented behaviour.

objections.claim: The spec's stated purpose for arm 1 is to stop re-narrowing — it claims the two-arm class "matches the whole YAML overlay-variant class" and covers "any future YAML overlay variant". But arm 1's segment class is `(?:\.[\w-]+)*`, which only admits **dot-prefixed** segments. A hyphen-joined variant spelling — `cat .faff/config-dev.yaml` — matches neither arm: arm 1 needs a `.` before each segment (after `config` the next char is `-`, so zero segments then `\.ya?ml` fails), and arm 2's lookahead `(?![\w.-])` rejects the `-`. That is exactly the same coverage-gap class the spec exists to close, one keystroke-style variant away from recurring. The spec pins this exact regex in DONE, so the builder cannot widen it during the build.
objections.evidence: §3 "The pattern" and the option-(c) rationale ("covers … any future YAML overlay variant"); §8 DONE item pinning `\.faff\/config(?:(?:\.[\w-]+)*\.ya?ml\b|(?![\w.-]))`.
objections.predicted_consequence: the first `config-<suffix>.yaml` overlay variant a team adopts is hand-readable undetected, and the guard re-narrows again — the precise regression this spec files against FAFF-1302.

objections.claim: The extensionless arm `(?![\w.-])` treats `/` as a permitted terminator, so the widened pattern flags reads of anything under a `.faff/config/` directory — exactly the "non-config reads whose path merely starts `.faff/config`" class the spec's design principles forbid.
objections.evidence: Spec §3, chosen pattern `\.faff\/config(?:(?:[.-][\w.-]*)?\.ya?ml\b|(?![\w.-]))`; the principle "The guard must NOT start flagging non-config reads whose path merely starts `.faff/config`". For `cat .faff/config/extra.yaml`, after `config` comes `/`, which is not in `[\w.-]`, so arm 2 matches — while the current pattern (`\.ya?ml` required immediately) does not. The spec's negative-case enumeration (`.json`, `.lock`, `-notes.md`, `configuration.yaml`) and its mandated unit-test case table both omit this class, so a builder following the spec verbatim ships it with green tests.
objections.predicted_consequence: A plausible future layout (config fragments under `.faff/config/`) makes the lint false-positive on legitimate reads; the mandated case table passes anyway, so the regression is invisible to the spec's own tests until a shipped `SKILL.md` or a fixture trips it. Fix is a one-character lookahead widening (`(?![\w.\-/])`) plus one negative case — a small in-place spec edit.

objections.claim: DONE requires "The canonical names (`.faff/config.yaml`, `.faff/config.local.yaml`) are still flagged (no regression)", and the HOW step says the unit test asserts "the full match/no-match case table below" — but the only enumerated cases (§5 scenarios) contain the dot-variant, hyphen-variant, extensionless, `.json`, prose, and `.example` cases. Neither canonical name appears as a positive case anywhere a tester can enumerate, so the "case table" the test must cover is not fully specified.
objections.evidence: DONE item "The canonical names … are still flagged (no regression)" vs the §5 scenario list, which never exercises `.faff/config.yaml` or `.faff/config.local.yaml`.
objections.predicted_consequence: a build could pass every named scenario and every named negative case while the rewritten two-arm pattern accidentally drops the original canonical matches (e.g. a botched variant group that no longer accepts the bare `.yaml` suffix), and the new unit test would still be green — the regression the DONE item explicitly guards is untested by the spec's own test plan.

objections.claim: The spec's first design principle is "Cover the whole variant class, not a fixed list," and the chosen two-arm pattern is justified as matching "exactly the config spellings (`.yaml`/`.yml` variants and the bare file)." But the two arms are disjoint in a way the spec never reconciles: arm 1 requires a mandatory `.ya?ml` suffix, and arm 2's lookahead `(?![\w.\-/])` rejects anything following `config` with a `.` — which is exactly what an extensionless *variant* begins with. So `cat .faff/config.local` and `cat .faff/config-dev` (no `.yaml` suffix) match neither arm and pass the guard silently. This is not hypothetical: FAFF-1302's own overlay file is `.faff/config.local.yaml`, and an extensionless spelling of it is the most sensitive file in the set (the overlay "may hold machine-local values" per the config-under-faff-dir tests) — precisely the file a hand-read guard exists to protect. The spec's case table omits every extensionless-variant row, so the unit test it mandates will never discover the gap; the DONE item "cover the whole variant class" is asserted by prose and contradicted by the pattern.
objections.evidence: §3 "The pattern" — arm 2 is `(?![\w.\-/])`, which cannot accept `.local`/`-dev` extensionless; the §3 case table has `cat .faff/config` (bare) but no `cat .faff/config.local` row; §1 principle "Cover the whole variant class, not a fixed list."
objections.predicted_consequence: a `SKILL.md` line `grep slots .faff/config.local` passes the FAFF-50 guard green while hand-reading the machine-local overlay — a fail-open path in the lint for the highest-sensitivity config file, invisible to the spec's own test because the case table doesn't enumerate it.

objections.claim: DONE requires "A `.faff/config.example.yaml` line is NOT flagged (existing `.example` line-skip)", but the §3 case table — which the DONE item says the unit test "asserts every row of" — contains no `.example` row. As specified, the test that pins the carve-out never exercises it; the carve-out's regression protection rests on scenario 5's prose only, and the spec's own "authoritative" framing of the table is undercut.
objections.evidence: DONE item "A `.faff/config.example.yaml` line is NOT flagged"; §3 case table (no `.example` row); §4 step 3 ("asserting the §3 case table, line by line").
objections.predicted_consequence: a build can pass the specified unit test while the `.example` line-skip has been dropped or reordered below the regex match, and the DONE item is checked off without any test deciding it.
